context: Canvas-rendered scatterplot of research output (publications) vs. years of experience for 1,500 synthetic researchers across 5 fields, with SVG axis overlay, keyboard accessibility, and a sortable data table toggle.
first_impression: Structurally honest scatter encoding with clean position-for-position, color-for-category mapping and no misleading size encoding, but hardcoded scale domains make it brittle under data changes.
what_works: Both axes start at 0 with appropriate domains for the data range; all points use fixed radius (3.5px) so no size encodes data — eliminating any lie-factor risk. D3 table join uses keyed data (.data(sorted, d => d.id)) for object constancy.
what_doesnt: Scale domains are hardcoded magic numbers ([0,36] and [0,210]) rather than derived from data via d3.max/d3.extent — fails the scaling and shift metamorphic relations (multiply all values by k and points leave the viewport). Quadtree spatial search uses data.indexOf(next) which is O(n) per keystroke, a minor robustness concern at scale.
